nodes.description: Only the first two genes of the X-linked array are expressed in the retina. In protans neither expressed gene encodes an L-class pigment: the expressed genes are normal OPN1MW copies or 5'L-3'M hybrids. Spectral tuning is dominated by exon 5, which accounts for a shift of roughly 15 to 25 nm, so a hybrid carrying M-type exon 5 encodes an M-class pigment whatever its 5' exons.

nodes.description: Commercial notch-filter (EnChroma) and other colour-enhancing (VINO) spectacles alter the relative stimulation of the remaining cones. They do not restore the missing L cone class. A controlled study found no overall improvement on clinical colour tests with EnChroma lenses; another found a functionally meaningful change on the CAD test only with VINO glasses. Tinted ChromaGen lenses reduced plate-test errors without reducing severity, and no protanope passed any test with them.

evidence.reference_title: Do EnChroma glasses improve performance on clinical tests for red-green color deficiencies?
evidence.snippet: Comparing the performance of 86 well-categorized CVD observers and 24 controls on two clinical tests we report no overall improvement when EnChroma lenses were worn.

evidence.reference_title: Effects of color-enhancing glasses on color vision in congenital red-green color deficiencies.
evidence.snippet: Although there was a statistically significant effect of both glasses, only that of VINO could be considered functionally meaningful.

evidence.reference_title: Color vision devices for color vision deficiency patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: This review concludes that commercially available color vision devices, such as EnChroma Glasses, Chromagen filters, and EnChroma Cx-14 do not provide clinically significant evidence that subjective color perception has improved.

evidence.reference_title: Impact of ChromaGen lenses on colour vision test performance of individuals with congenital colour vision deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The dichromatic individuals showed minimal improvement, with none of the participants with protanopia passing any of the tests using any ChromaGen lens.

nodes.description: Protan retinas contain M-class and S cones but no functional L cones. Fundus reflectometry and electroretinography in X-linked dichromats fit a replacement model, in which the total number of cones is unchanged and the missing cone class is replaced by the remaining one. Cone-resolved optoretinography shows that the remaining M and S cones respond normally.

nodes.description: Red-green colour discrimination depends on comparing signals from two cone classes in the middle-to-long wavelength range. When both expressed pigments are spectrally identical (protanopia) the comparison is impossible and vision is dichromatic; when they differ by a few nanometres (protanomaly) a weak signal remains. Severity is inversely related to the spectral separation between the two expressed pigments. Left unbound to GO: the nearest process term, GO:0007601 visual perception, is broader than red-green opponent comparison and an OLS label/synonym search of GO for "color vision", "colour vision", "color discrimination" and "color perception" returned no terms.

nodes.description: Because the remaining cones carry M-class pigment, protans are relatively insensitive to long-wavelength light; red lights look dim and are seen at a shorter range. In laboratory spectral sensitivity data every protan had lower red-light sensitivity than the least sensitive colour-normal observer, which bears on recognition of red signal lights and on occupational and driving standards.

evidence.reference_title: Protan colour vision deficiency and road accidents.
evidence.snippet: A laboratory study of the spectral sensitivity of protan and colour normal subjects that largely removes these sources' variability shows that all protans have a sensitivity to red light that is less than that of the least sensitive colour normal.

evidence.reference_title: Protan colour vision deficiency and road accidents.
evidence.snippet: Field trial data show that protans have a very reduced visual range for red signals compared to colour normal observers

evidence.reference_title: Traffic signal color recognition is a problem for both protan and deutan color-vision deficients.
evidence.snippet: response times of deuteranopes and protanopes were 53% and 35% longer than those of color normals

nodes.description: The L and M pigments share 96% amino acid identity and their genes sit in a head-to-tail tandem array. Misalignment of the arrays in female meiosis followed by an intergenic or intragenic crossover (unequal homologous recombination, with gene conversion as a further route) yields arrays that have lost OPN1LW or carry a 5'L-3'M hybrid gene in its place. This germline rearrangement is the initiating lesion for most protan defects; rarer routes include inactivating OPN1LW exon 3 haplotypes and truncating variants.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular basis of variation in human color vision.
evidence.snippet: The high homology between these genes has predisposed the locus to relatively common unequal recombination events that give rise to red/green hybrid genes and to deletion of the green-pigment genes. Such events constitute the most common cause of red-green color vision defects.
